title: 2008 AMC 10A Problem 20
statement: Trapezoid \(ABCD\) has bases \(AB\) and \(CD\) and diagonals intersecting at \(K.\) Suppose that \(AB = 9,\) \(DC = 12,\) and the area of \(\triangle AKD\) is \(24.\) What is the area of trapezoid \(ABCD?\)

solutions.text:
Triangles \(AKB\) and \(CKD\) are similar with ratio \(\dfrac{9}{12} = \dfrac{3}{4}.\)

Since \(\triangle AKD\) and \(\triangle KCD\) have bases \(AK\) and \(KC\) on the same line and share the same altitude from \(D,\) \(\dfrac{[KCD]}{[AKD]} = \dfrac{KC}{AK} = \dfrac{4}{3},\) so \([KCD] = 32.\) Similarly \([AKB] = 18.\)

Also \([BKC] = [AKD] = 24.\) The total is \(24 + 32 + 18 + 24 = 98.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Triangles \(AKB\) and \(CKD\) are similar with ratio \(9 : 12\)
\(\triangle AKD\) and \(\triangle BKC\) have equal areas; scale the others from \([AKD] = 24\)
